title: Verify Payment Due Reminder is Sent on Schedule
description: This test validates that the automated credit card payment due reminder is sent to the cardholder on time, ensuring timely notification and compliance with the requirement to help prevent late fees. Automation: HIGH — notifications can be asserted via API response or email receipt.
testDescription: A cardholder with an active credit card account is approaching their scheduled payment due date. The system must automatically trigger and send a payment due reminder notification, including only the last 4 digits of the card number, to the registered notification channel (email, SMS, or portal).
prerequisites: Active cardholder account exists in the database, cardholder has a valid email address or notification channel configured, future payment due date is set in account profile, backend notification service is operational
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in as cardholder to the portal or mobile app. 2. Confirm card details and notification settings are correct. 3. Query the upcoming payment due date from the account profile. 4. Simulate time advancement (or wait) to the scheduled notification trigger window (e.g., 3 days before due date). 5. Poll backend or scheduled job queue to verify notification is queued. 6. Check cardholder's email inbox or notification channel. 7. Locate payment reminder notification with correct sender and subject. 8. Verify notification content includes only the last 4 digits of the card and the due date. 9. Confirm no other portions of the card number are displayed. 10. Validate the notification timestamp matches the system schedule.
expectedResult: 1. Payment due reminder is received on or before the scheduled window. 2. Notification includes only the last 4 digits of card number (e.g., **** **** **** 4242). 3. No other part of the card number appears. 4. Notification delivery timestamp aligns with system defined schedule.

sourceCitation.excerpt: An automated notification is sent to the cardholder reminding them of their upcoming credit card payment due date

title: Ensure Only Last 4 Digits Displayed in Due Reminder

prerequisites: Cardholder account exists with credit card ending in 5678, notification service enabled, test environment configured to monitor outbound notifications
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in as cardholder to portal or mobile app. 2. Confirm account profile lists card ending in 5678. 3. Trigger or simulate due reminder notification (advance due date or execute scheduled job). 4. Access cardholder's email inbox or notification channel. 5. Locate due reminder notification. 6. Inspect notification subject and body for card number presence. 7. Verify that only '5678' appears for card identification. 8. Search for any additional card digit presence in notification. 9. Check application and notification logs for card number exposure. 10. Confirm notification records do not contain full or partial card numbers.
expectedResult: 1. Notification displays only '5678' as card identifier. 2. No other digits or PAN segments appear anywhere in notification or logs. 3. No PII/PCI leakage in any notification, email header, or backend log.

title: Verify Due Reminder Delivered via Email Channel
description: Verifies that a due reminder is automatically sent to the cardholder before payment due date, and the notification email contains only the last 4 digits of the credit card number for identification, ensuring data privacy compliance. Automation: HIGH — pure notification content and delivery assertion.
testDescription: A cardholder nearing their payment due date should receive a reminder email. This test ensures the email is delivered, that it is formatted correctly with only the last 4 digits of the card, and that no other digits or sensitive information are present.
prerequisites: Cardholder account exists with next payment due within 3 days, valid cardholder email configured, notification service and SMTP enabled, no prior reminder sent for this cycle.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in to the cardholder portal as the test cardholder. 2. Confirm account is active and payment due in next 3 days. 3. Wait for system to trigger the due reminder notification (scheduled batch or real-time). 4. Check the recipient's email inbox (test+user123@example.com) for new reminder message. 5. Open the received email. 6. Verify subject and body reference the due date and card ending in specified last 4 digits (e.g., 'Card ending 4242'). 7. Search the email content to ensure no other part (beginning, middle, or masked) of the card number is present. 8. Review headers/attachments to ensure only last 4 digits appear in all included fields. 9. Check notification system logs/audit for notification event containing only last 4 digits as identifier. 10. Log out from the portal.
expectedResult: Due reminder is delivered to correct email address; email body and metadata display only last 4 digits of the card; no other part of the credit card number or PII is present.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Credit Card Due Reminder: An automated notification is sent to the cardholder...should include the last 4 digits of the credit card number

title: Verify Overdue Alert Delivered via Portal
description: Checks that when a cardholder misses their payment, an overdue alert is triggered and posted to the portal, displaying only the last 4 digits of the credit card number. Protects against data privacy violations and alerts the user to overdue status. Automation: HIGH — portal and notification content check.
testDescription: After the cardholder misses their payment due date, the system posts an overdue alert to their online portal. The alert must contain only the last 4 digits of the credit card number and specify overdue amount and consequences. The test ensures the alert is present and formatted according to requirements.
prerequisites: Cardholder account exists and missed payment due date, portal access enabled, overdue alert logic configured and active, no prior overdue alert dismissed.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in to the cardholder portal as the test user. 2. Confirm account status shows as overdue. 3. Navigate to the notifications or alerts section. 4. Locate overdue alert in the UI (typically with timestamp after due date). 5. Open or expand the alert to view full content. 6. Verify the alert includes the last 4 digits of the credit card number (e.g., 'Card ending 6589'). 7. Check that the overdue balance and warning of potential consequences are displayed. 8. Search content to ensure no other digits or segments of the credit card number are present. 9. Validate no full credit card number or PII is shown in page source or tooltips. 10. Log out from the portal.
expectedResult: Overdue alert visible in portal on overdue accounts; alert shows only last 4 digits of cardnumber; no additional credit card digits or PII present in content or metadata.

sourceCitation.excerpt: alert is sent to notify them of the overdue balance...should include the last 4 digits of the credit card number.

title: Verify Collection Notification Delivered via Letter
description: Confirms that when an account is significantly delinquent, the system generates and delivers a formal collection letter that includes only the last 4 digits of the credit card number, in compliance with data privacy standards. Automation: MEDIUM — may require integration with document or print testing.
testDescription: When the cardholder account becomes seriously delinquent, the system sends a formal collection notification by postal mail. The letter must detail the amount owed, extra charges, and reference the card only by its last 4 digits, never the full or partially masked number.
prerequisites: Delinquent cardholder account exists (payment missed for >30 days), postal address on file, automated collection workflow enabled, mail merge/letter generation service operational.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in to the issuer's admin interface as a collections agent. 2. Filter for accounts in 'significantly delinquent' state. 3. Select target cardholder account. 4. Trigger or verify generation of formal collection letter (PDF or print). 5. Download or view the generated letter/document. 6. Review salutation and identifying info for reference to last 4 digits only (e.g., 'Account: ****6589'). 7. Confirm the body details all required amounts, dates, and next actions. 8. Search entire letter for any segment or presence of full credit card number. 9. Review storage and transmission logs to ensure only last 4 digits appear in communications and system actions. 10. Log out from the admin interface.
expectedResult: Formal collection letter references only last 4 digits; no other card number digits or PII present in document, attachments, or print job; compliance with privacy mandate is maintained.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Collection Notification ... sending formal collection notifications to the cardholder...should include the last 4 digits of the credit card number.

title: Verify Legal Action Notice Delivered via External Correspondence
description: Verifies that a legal action notice is generated for accounts undergoing legal escalation, and that the external legal correspondence includes only the last 4 digits of the credit card number to comply with privacy and legal requirements. Automation: MEDIUM — depends on external document delivery validation.
testDescription: When a cardholder’s delinquent account is escalated to legal action, the bank generates formal legal documentation (e.g., lawsuit, court notice) sent by external means. The documentation must reference the cardholder only by last 4 digits and include no other part of the card number, both in document body and headers.
prerequisites: Cardholder account in legal escalation state, legal documentation workflow active, external correspondence channel (mail/courier) configured, legal notice generation service available.
stepsToPerform: 1. As an authorized legal support user, log into the admin/legal portal. 2. Filter/select accounts flagged for legal action initiation. 3. Trigger generation of legal action notification/notice. 4. Retrieve the generated legal notice file intended for external delivery. 5. Review header, formal addressee, and case reference sections for card identification. 6. Confirm last 4 digits of credit card are present, with no other digits. 7. Review full document to verify absence of any full or partial credit card numbers. 8. Validate document meta, cover sheets, and attachments for card number exposure. 9. Check back-end audit logs/print logs for references; ensure no more than last 4 digits visible. 10. Log out from the legal portal.
expectedResult: Legal action notice delivered externally references only the last 4 digits of the credit card number; no other part of the number or PII exposes cardholder data; system remains compliant.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Any legal documentation should include the last 4 digits of the credit card number

title: End-to-End: Payment Lifecycle from Due Reminder to Legal Action
description: Covers the complete end-to-end journey from an account's due reminder, through missed payment, overdue and collection notifications, payment plan proposal, collection agency involvement, to legal escalation. Validates that only last 4 digits of the card number appear at every stage. Critical for regulatory and business integrity. Automation: MEDIUM — requires orchestration of state transitions, multi-user, and multi-channel validation.
testDescription: A credit card account begins in a normal state, becomes overdue after missing payment, passes through overdue/collection notifications, receives a payment plan proposal (and does not accept), escalates to collections with agency involvement, and finally proceeds to legal action. Test ensures each notification/document at every stage contains only last 4 digits of the card number, all escalations trigger the correct content, and privacy/compliance is upheld throughout.
prerequisites: Active cardholder account in good standing, automated workflows for all notification and escalation steps enabled, valid contact channels (email, address), test accounts for collections agent and legal support roles configured.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in as the cardholder and confirm upcoming due date. 2. Allow system to trigger and send due reminder email; log out. 3. After due date passes without payment, log in as the cardholder and confirm account moves to overdue state; view portal for overdue alert notification. 4. Wait until delinquency threshold passes, then log in as collections agent and trigger/send formal collection notification by letter. 5. Confirm receipt of collection letter (test address/integration validation). 6. After no payment is received, verify payment plan proposal is generated and sent to cardholder email/portal (do not accept, let time elapse). 7. Card remains unpaid and escalates to collections agency; log in as agency user and retrieve case ID, verifying communication references only last 4 digits. 8. Without resolution, system auto-initiates legal action — legal support user logs in, generates and reviews formal legal documentation. 9. At every notification/document retrieval (steps 2,3,5,6,7,8), review content to confirm only last 4 digits are present, and confirm full/partial credit card number is nowhere exposed. 10. Log out from all user roles (cardholder, collections agent, agency, legal).
expectedResult: At every stage — due reminder, overdue alert, collection notification, payment plan proposal, agency communication, and legal documentation — only the last 4 digits of the credit card number are present in user-facing notifications and documents. No full or partial PAN is ever disclosed; all privacy rules enforced across the full lifecycle.
